routes.identity: Taylor Brown, exactly second place/runner-up in US Big Brother season 28; top-two, finalist, eviction and winner are distinct.
differences: BIGBROTHERRANK pp1–3 uses official final rank, includes final reinstatement, allows rank inference from elimination structure and shared double evictions. Its first official ranking controls later alterations. PM RTC and the exact listing require an official second-place outcome; generic elimination finality must not be substituted for final placement.

Kalshi gives a listed Tie strike priority; without one it splits shared ranks at cents. PM mutually exclusive successful outcomes split at its tick (currently cents). Presence and precedence of a Tie strike are a condition, not assumed absent.

Kalshi cancellation/truncation without final ranks pays No. PM may use fair-price/review cancellation and amends finale expiration. Kalshi administrative date is December 31 with latest January 7, despite PM’s October 1 finale label.

Withdrawal counts only if an official final second-place rank remains on Kalshi; PM’s generic withdrawal provision is explicitly for winner contracts, so placement handling needs an unambiguous official result.
conditions: Unique official final second-place ranking, no joint rank/elimination inference/withdrawal dispute, cancellation or deadline divergence.

routes.identity: Anthropic IPO confirmation by September 30, 2026 11:59 PM ET versus before October 1; company and intended cutoff align at date granularity.
differences: Kalshi short primary text lists effective SEC S-1, pricing, or exchange ticker assignment. The linked WHENIPO/IPOEventConfirm pp1–2 expands to foreign equivalent approvals and requires ticker plus approved IPO listing, substantially matching PM IPCC pp2–3. Do not claim foreign-regulator incompatibility solely from the shortened listing.

The short Kalshi ticker-assignment clause is broader than the linked document. Contract precedence at that boundary is not resolved here. Both long documents exclude filing alone, direct listings without new shares, SPAC/reverse merger, private offers and non-common-equity listings.

Kalshi long terms additionally require a first-time public listing and enumerate prior-public/OTC/relisting exclusions. PM’s reviewed product lacks the same explicit first-time history test. Any prior-public history or nonstandard issuance needs confirmation.

PM explicitly fixes 11:59 PM ET; Kalshi says before October 1 with 11:59 PM trading time. Exact final-minute inclusion remains unresolved. Kalshi expected expiration April 1, 2027 is later than its October 8 latest expiration; PM lists July 15, 2027. These administrative anomalies preclude a reliable short capital-lockup estimate.
conditions: Resolve short-versus-long trigger precedence, exact cutoff, company public-listing history and contradictory administrative horizons before strategy admission.
routes.lockupBasis: Contract cutoff only; administrative horizons conflict and do not support a fund-release estimate.
